plan: My value is $10. In a single-round game with unknown opponent strategies, I want to bid strategically. Since the second-highest bid determines my payment if I win, I'll aim to bid slightly above my true value but not excessively. Other bidders might also try to bid near their value. A bid around $11-$12 seems reasonable - high enough to potentially win, but not so high that I risk significant loss if my value is low.

My value is $30. In a first-price sealed bid auction, rational strategy involves considering others' likely behavior. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0-$49, other bidders will likely bid strategically near their own values. I want to win without overpaying. A bid around my value's midpoint ($15) seems reasonable - high enough to have a good chance of winning, but low enough to potentially generate profit if I win at a lower price than my true value.

My value is $25. In a first-price sealed bid auction, optimal strategy involves balancing potential profit against risk of overbidding. Since my value is mid-range, I'll bid strategically near my value. Others likely have random values between $0-$49. I'll bid slightly below my true value to create a buffer against potential loss.
